title: Coupled Restart, Split-Run & Replay Composition — Architecture Invariant Audit
scope: Owner-side qualification of committed-boundary coupled restart, fresh-process restore and replay composition. This is not independent qualification, canonical admission, MultiSWAP scaling qualification, a whole-window sensitivity qualification, or full groundwater-coupling-v1 closure.
key_findings: The production restart seam is typed and serialization-neutral; file/path/format I/O exists only in the qualification harness.
Only committed SWAP state, committed groundwater continuation state, committed interface-ledger state and coupling-origin provenance cross the restart boundary.

Groundwater candidate tokens, pending candidate times, prepared publication reservations, ledger trial exchanges, solver scratch, Newton/Jacobian state and other transient publication credentials are not persisted.
Restart export is fail-closed while the groundwater exchange service has a live prepared reservation or the mass ledger has an active trial/prepared transaction.
Groundwater restart adapter metadata is cross-checked against an actual service checkpoint for service identity, lineage, revision and committed time.
Restore is staged so recoverable validation and adapter rejection occur before local SWAP, ledger and coupling-origin publication.

After an adapter reports successful external restore, violated groundwater postconditions are fail-hard rather than returned as a recoverable status, preventing an externally mutated backend from coexisting with an apparently rollbackable local result.
The true split-process path is byte-identical to the uninterrupted two-window path under both O0 and O2, and O0/O2 signatures are identical.
The exercised predictor-corrector path retains exact interface action-reaction mass conservation; F-GC24 introduces no mass tolerance.
No direct MODFLOW implementation, tile aggregation, deep-vadose transfer, whole-window response tangent, large-batch scaling or bounded-cost integration claim is made.

invariants.assessment: Restart composes the common SWAP kernel committed-state persistence seam; it creates no use-case-specific kernel.
Production restart runtime contains no file/path/parser/file-unit persistence format; external serialization is deliberately outside the kernel/runtime contract.
SWAP committed physical state, groundwater continuation state, mass ledger and coupling origin remain explicit separate typed data categories.
Only continuation-relevant committed state and provenance are persisted; transient candidate/prepared tokens and solver scratch are excluded.
No Newton vectors, Jacobians, constitutive intermediates or worker scratch are added to persistent column state.
The restart carrier is logical/typed and does not prescribe per-column heavyweight solver ownership or an AoS memory layout.

Restart is accepted-boundary only; export rejects live prepared/trial work, recoverable restore failures leave local committed carriers unpublished, and successful external restore postcondition violations fail hard.
Continuation reconstructs the same committed physical origin; no rejected trial is promoted as physical state.
Committed time is a generic finite coordinate; no day/month/year or midnight semantics are encoded.
Restart records an accepted generic coupling-window boundary and imposes no fixed coupling-window duration.
Coupling provenance, groundwater continuation, ledger continuation and transactional publication semantics are explicit runtime responsibilities.
F-GC24 preserves the admitted typed direct-groundwater interface and does not change H/q sign or residual semantics.
Committed interface-ledger continuation is restored exactly and the qualified replay path retains exact zero action-reaction residual; no configurable mass concession is introduced.
Restart does not remove or reinterpret interface-sensitivity output; whole-window sensitivity composition remains an explicit separate F-GC23 obligation.
Restart/replay adds no finite-difference coupling rerun requirement and does not change the predictor-plus-corrector normal route.
No per-column heavyweight restart solver object is introduced; this is compatibility evidence only, not a 100k-column scaling qualification.
No one-to-one MODFLOW-cell mapping or tile fraction is encoded in persisted SWAP state.
No deep-vadose state or transfer law is embedded in SWAP restart; such a component can remain external.
F-GC24 neither creates nor destroys transfer-zone storage; committed interface mass remains explicit and conserved across replay.
Restart targets common committed-state/runtime contracts rather than a specific Richards implementation.
Existing SWAP and coupling physics are reused unchanged; this workunit adds continuation composition only.
No HeadCalc-private arrays or numerical internals enter the restart contract.
No physical option is changed by restart policy; physical configuration and numerical/restart mechanics remain separate.
No unbounded retry or hidden recomputation is added. Bounded-cost MultiSWAP coupling remains a separate F-GC26 qualification obligation.
Reference mode and existing full-accuracy solver paths are not modified or removed.

Restart status, provenance rejection, service quiescence, ledger quiescence and fail-hard adapter-contract violations are explicit and test-visible; complete large-batch coupling diagnostics remain separate work.
Groundwater restart state exists only for compositions that instantiate the restart adapter; no global optional-state tax is introduced.
The runtime/coupler supplies the groundwater service and separate restart adapter; SWAP does not know backend file formats, MODFLOW cell fractions or transfer-zone topology.
No hidden .swp, path, midnight, one-day or direct-MODFLOW assumption is introduced in production restart code.
This artifact explicitly checks all 30 architecture invariants; owner qualification and later independent/canonical gates remain separate.

nonclaims: No full Groundwater Coupling v1 completion claim.
No real MODFLOW/aquifer restart adapter qualification.
No F-GC23 accepted whole-window response-tangent qualification.
No F-GC26 bounded-cost response-aware integration qualification.
